critical_code_review_comments: TradeChart.jsx:845 uses `off < 0` as the browsing predicate. That correctly matches the intent 'newest candle scrolled off to the right', but on very narrow panes where BASE_RIGHT_OFFSET(8) exceeds maxBars, the live-follow block itself clamps `want` down; in that edge case dataset.liveFollow may stay '1' with a slightly reduced parked offset — jumpToLive() still works via scrollToRealTime(). No user-visible issue observed at 1920x1080.

jumpToLive() only sets followRef.current = true; the RAF then updates browsingRef + setBrowsingHistory(false) on the next frame. There's a ~16-33ms window where a click could theoretically be double-registered — not observed, and the CaretRight arrow visibly disappears well under 200ms in tests.

Button placement is CSS-fixed via right-[68px]/bottom-[46px] Tailwind literals — hardcoded pixel gutters for the price axis (right) and time axis (bottom). If either axis width becomes dynamic (e.g. price format changes to 8 decimals for crypto) the button could overlap. Consider anchoring to the price/time-axis container refs instead of magic numbers.
